instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbyists who meet the threshold must file bi-monthly reports, not annual spending reports.
The statute sets bi-monthly reporting periods and does not require monthly lobbyist spending reports.
The lobbyist periodic spending report is required on a bi-monthly cadence, which is an 'other' frequency.
Reporting is bi-monthly (six periods per year), not quarterly.
Semi-annual reports are filed by clients, while lobbyists file bi-monthly reports under § 1-h.
The statute specifies bi-monthly periods rather than three-times-per-year (tri-annual) reports.

cell.value: Bi-monthly (every two months; due the 15th day after each Jan-Feb, Mar-Apr, May-Jun, Jul-Aug, Sep-Oct, Nov-Dec period).

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-h(a) lists six two-month reporting periods and requires filing by the 15th day after each period ends.
Lobbyist bi-monthly reports must itemize expenses over $75 by amount, payee, and purpose (with names when on behalf of one person), indicating itemized expense disclosure.
Lobbyists must file bi-monthly spending reports (six times per year), which is not one of the standard annual/semiannual/quarterly/monthly options.
The lobbyist’s bi-monthly report must include legislative bill numbers and executive order identifiers/subject matter and other specific matters lobbied.
Bi-monthly lobbyist reports must state the compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist.
The bi-monthly report requires identifying matters lobbied and the body before which lobbying occurred, but it does not require disclosure of specific contacts/communications.
Section 1-h requires compensation and expenses reporting but does not require allocating expenditures by issue/bill.
Lobbyists must report a description of the general subject or subjects on which they have lobbied.
The bi-monthly report includes the general subject or subjects lobbied, satisfying the Tier 0 'general subjects' activity disclosure.
The statute excludes the lobbyist’s personal sustenance, lodging and travel disbursements from reportable expenses, so such 'other costs' are not comprehensively required components.
Lobbyists must report expenses incurred for lobbying (with certain exclusions) and aggregate non-lobbyist salary expenses, covering non-compensation/indirect lobbying costs.
Lobbyists’ bi-monthly reports include their identity, client, issues/bill numbers, and compensation plus expenses, meeting the described itemized spending/compensation disclosure elements.
The bi-monthly report must contain the lobbyist’s name, address and telephone number.
Lobbyists must report bill numbers and executive order identifiers/subject matter, which is disclosure of specific legislation/executive actions being influenced.
The bi-monthly lobbyist report requires client identification but does not require stating whether the principal is public or private or describing the nature of its business.
Lobbyists must disclose the client’s name, address and telephone number.
Each bi-monthly report lists the client by whom or on whose behalf the lobbyist is retained, employed, or designated.
The bi-monthly report must include the legislative bill numbers of any bills on which the lobbyist has lobbied.
The report requires disclosure of compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist, i.e., direct lobbying costs (compensation).
Lobbyists must report compensation paid or owed and expenses expended/received/incurred for lobbying, which provides total spending components toward lobbying for the period.
Because lobbyists file bi-monthly reports with issues/bill numbers and itemized expenses over $75 plus compensation, the regime meets the 'YES/MODERATE' criteria rather than having no such law.
Lobbyist spending reports require reporting of lobbying compensation/expenses but do not specifically require reporting spending on household members of public officials.
Expenses over $75 must be detailed by amount, payee, and purpose (and sometimes beneficiary name), requiring itemized rather than purely lump-sum disclosure.
